implementation_notes: kotlinx.coroutines supplies fork/join under structured concurrency: coroutineScope { } defines the lifetime, async { } starts each branch as a child coroutine returning Deferred, and awaitAll joins the fan-out - failing fast and cancelling siblings if any child throws, which is the error policy a recursive decomposition usually wants. Dispatch CPU-bound branches to Dispatchers.Default (the shared CPU dispatcher); Dispatchers.IO is for blocking calls and will not speed up arithmetic. Below the cut-off call the leaf function directly, because a coroutine hop per leaf costs more than the leaf itself.
pitfalls: Without a supervisor scope, one failing child cancels the whole scope (and its siblings) - deliberate for a pure reduction, surprising when partial results are acceptable.
A blocking call (JDBC, Thread.sleep, file I/O) inside Dispatchers.Default starves the shared CPU dispatcher; use Dispatchers.IO for blocking leaves.
async launched outside a scope (GlobalScope) or a Job smuggled into the context loses the join: children outlive the caller and the recursion leaks.
